title: 1977 AHSME Problem 28
statement: Let \(g(x)=x^5+x^4+x^3\) \({}+x^2+x+1.\) What is the remainder when the polynomial \(g(x^{12})\) is divided by the polynomial \(g(x)?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(R(x)\) be the remainder, so \(\deg R\le4.\) The five roots \(\alpha\) of \(g\) satisfy \(\alpha^6=1\) and \(\alpha\ne1.\) Hence \(\alpha^{12}=1\) and \[ R(\alpha)=g(\alpha^{12})=g(1)=6. \] Therefore \(R(x)-6,\) a polynomial of degree at most \(4,\) has five distinct roots. It must be identically zero, so \(R(x)=6.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is A.
hints: Evaluate the remainder at the five roots of \(g\) and use its degree bound
